 by Timothy Abraham
 How's stat?! published at 04:25 GMT 04:25 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images In his 46 ODI innings, this is only the third time Ben Duckett has been dismissed while playing a cut shot. He has been particularly effective with the shot, averaging 62 (90 average before today) at a strike-rate of 123.

 Eng 56-1 published at 11 overs 11 overs 
 Jack Edwards into the attack. To quote my colleague Marc Higginson, he is the latest in a line of Australian all-rounders who look like they don't particularly enjoy bowling.
 Edwards certainly has a weary expression during his opening over, even if it only costs him a couple of singles.

 Michael Vaughan 
Former England captain on Test Match Special 
 That was right under his nose, really full. Joe Root didn't have to do a lot with this one, just show the face of the blade and the outfield is quick.
 10 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 54-1 published at 10 overs 10 overs 
 Classic Joe Root.
 Impeccable timing from the England great as he stylishly drives a slightly full delivery from Spencer Johnson wide of mid-off for four.
 Worth the admission fee at the Adelaide Oval.
 Image source, Cricviz

 If Ben Duckett was born in Australia he’d never have played a game of professional cricket. Simply not suited to Australia conditions and can’t adapt.
 Will, South Wales 
 Lil Ducky will have to deal with pace and bounce at Wanderers and Centurion…
 Hardeep Nahal, London 
 9 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 48-1 published at 9 overs 9 overs 
 Joe Root gets off strike with a streaky inside edge off Xavier Bartlett .
 Meanwhile, Tom Banton is sufficiently distracted by a bird on the pitch to take a moment to chase it away waggling his bat like a gameskeeper chasing away a poacher.
 Bartlett bangs it in short to Banton who top edges it over wicketkeeper Josh Inglis' head for four.
 9 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 04:11 GMT 04:11 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images In the 28 matches he had captained before today, Harry Brook had won 13 tosses and lost 15 (29 matches and lost 16 tosses if we include today). 
 When he has won the toss, England won eight matches and lost five. 
 However, when he lost the toss, England won just five matches and lost 10. 
 Harry Brook as ODI Captain (29 matches) 
 Toss won: 13 – Matches won: 8 | Lost: 5 
 Toss lost: 16* – Matches won: 5 | Lost: 10 
 *Today's result is pending. 
 3 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 41-1 published at 8 overs 8 overs 
 A steady start for England who are quietly building a platform.
 11 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 04:10 GMT 04:10 GMT 
 Michael Vaughan 
Former England captain on Test Match Special 
 If Jack Edwards was at short leg, he might have taken that first boundary from Tom Banton but it was Travis Head and it's gone over his yellow cap to the boundary.
 5 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 41-1 published at 7.4 overs 7.4 overs 
 Image source, Getty Images Gasps from the Adelaide Oval crowd.
 Tom Banton pulls Spencer Johnson through mid-wicket for four.
 But it's aerial and Travis Head, acrobatically, leaps with a hand in the air but it goes just over him.
 No such worries a couple of balls later when Banton hooks Johnson over the boundary for six - England's first of the innings.
 Not completely timed by Banton, but he has got enough on it.
 17 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 04:06 GMT 04:06 GMT 
 Darren Lehmann 
Ex-Australia coach on Test Match Special 
 To win World Cups, your top four or five batters have to win the World Cup for you. You can't rely on numbers six, seven and eight. You need to get your bowing attack right for each condition. 
 England's top four or five looks really solid - Ben Duckett, Joe Root, Harry Brook and Jos Buttler.
 7 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 30-1 published at 7 overs 7 overs 
 Shottttt.
 Tom Banton thumps Xavier Bartlett's fourth delivery straight down the ground for four.
 Pure timing from the England opener.

 Image source, Getty Images Why does our team forget how to bat when we go to Australia? We could play their academy teams and still lose. I haven’t seen a run-rate this poor since 2015 in the pre-Morgan era.
 Arjun Singh, Edmonton, Canada

 Eng 25-1 published at 6 overs 6 overs 
 Tom Banton knows where he is, the administrative capital of Buckinghamshire, and is fit to continue.
 Joe Root with a nice clip through mid-wicket off the final ball of the over and he and Banton scamper three.

 A concussion check is required.

 Duckett could not have picked out Cooper Connolly any better. He just had to get down low and take it below his eyes.

 WICKET published at 4.5 overs 4.5 overs 
 Duckett c Connolly b Bartlett 9 (Eng 19-1) 
 Image source, Getty Images Having survived an lbw shout, Ben Duckett perishes a few deliveries later.
 In truth, it's a very tame dismissal for the England opener.
 He cuts rather loosely at a short-ish, slightly wider, delivery from Xavier Bartlett and ends up pinging it to Cooper Connolly at point.
